explain_example.question: How can I enable dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 networking in a local test cluster?

answer.name: kind CLI

closest.text: How do I create a local Kubernetes cluster with kind?

answer.reason: The kind CLI creates local Kubernetes clusters in container nodes. Dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 is enabled through kind's cluster networking configuration (ipFamily: dual), so the existing tool covers the request without new building.

candidates.name: kindnetd CNI Daemon
candidates.reason: kindnetd is the internal CNI daemon that kind runs inside its nodes. Its description covers pod CIDR routing, CNI config and masquerading, but nothing about enabling IPv6 or dual-stack, and a developer does not enable dual-stack by using it

candidates.name: AKS Extension Commands

closest.text: How do I set up Kaito on a cluster?

candidates.reason: AKS extension commands manage Azure-hosted AKS clusters from VS Code. The request is about a local test cluster, so this does not apply.

candidates.name: kind CLI

closest.text: How do I create a local Kubernetes cluster with kind?

candidates.reason: The kind CLI creates local Kubernetes clusters in container nodes. Dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 is enabled through kind's cluster networking configuration (ipFamily: dual), so the existing tool covers the request without new building.

candidates.name: github.com/grafana/ckit
candidates.reason: ckit is a clustering and workload distribution library using consistent hashing and gossip. It has no connection to Kubernetes cluster networking or dual-stack setup.
